chunks: By Allah, whatever the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) told them, I am here telling you the same today.
And what you hear today is not different from what they heard yesterday.
And the eyes that were opened for them and the hearts that were made for them at that time, just the same have been given to you at this time.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between the spiritual capacity of the Prophet's companions and the Imams according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) asserts that the spiritual capacity and divine knowledge granted to the companions of the Prophet were identical to those granted to him, emphasizing that the sensory and intellectual faculties (eyes and hearts) used by the Prophet's companions to receive revelation and wisdom are the same faculties possessed by the listeners in his time. This establishes a continuity of spiritual authority and understanding, reinforcing the Shia doctrine of the unbroken transmission of *'ilm* (knowledge) and the validity of the Imams' interpretive authority as the direct heirs to the Prophet's inner knowledge. The statement serves as a foundational argument for the reliability of the Ahl al-Bayt's teachings, linking the era of revelation directly to the era of the Imams.

en.sayed-ali-raza: By Allāh, whatever the Prophet told them, I am here telling you the same
and whatever you hear today is not different from what they heard yesterday.
The eyes that were opened for them and the hearts that were made for them at that time, just the same have been given to you at this time.
